subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw support for openclaw.json, auth-profile SQLite storage, generated residues, and backups?
rationale: The code path is source-reproducible, but the permanent fix changes key custody, unattended startup, recovery, rotation, migrations, and auth/provider compatibility, so automation should not choose it without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Design native encrypted-at-rest storage
options.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus auth-profile storage.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as the supported mitigation
options.body: Decide that transparent native encryption is out of scope for now and narrow this issue to docs, audit guidance, and SecretRef migration coverage.

options.title: Land partial hardening first
options.body: Use a smaller auth-store or resolver-backed step while explicitly keeping the broader credential-at-rest tracker open for key management and migration coverage.

recommendation.title: Design native encrypted-at-rest storage
recommendation.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus auth-profile storage.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal across auth-profile persistence and config write behavior, which are the central migration surfaces.
